text: Good catch, you're right that most keys shouldn't have usage if only one were in play. From the engine's usage.json: the first 9 keys are spent (0-1 credits left, some marked 'monthly credits used up'), so the pool walked down the list and tried them. That fits keys 10-14 each showing only about 15 calls (45-60 credits) spread over many hours. But one key (e4d5beb03d) has 1,386 calls for only 76 credits, which is odd. That points to the calls being refused or free, not paid reads. I haven't found the cause. My leading guesses are that each new engine job re-tries the spent keys first, or that the usage reads touch each key. I'll trace it and fix it so a job starts on the first key that still has credits and stays there.
